cases.sentence: – Нынче утром Лиза заезжала ко мне – они еще не боятся ездить ко мне, несмотря на графиню Лидию Ивановну, – вставила она, – и рассказывала про ваш ___.
cases.explain: «афинский вечер» — after the preposition «про», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “This morning Liza came to see me—they’re not afraid to call on me, in spite of the Countess Lidia Ivanovna,” she put in—“and she told me about your Athenian evening. How loathsome!”

cases.sentence: – Да, да, – сказала она, видимо стараясь отогнать ___. – Но если бы ты знал, как мне тяжело!
cases.explain: «ревнивые мысли» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Yes, yes,” she said, evidently trying to suppress her jealous thoughts. “But if only you knew how wretched I am! I believe you, I believe you. … What were you saying?”

cases.sentence: – Ах, невыносимо! – сказал он, стараясь уловить нить потерянной мысли. – Он не выигрывает от ___.
cases.explain: «близкого знакомства» — after the preposition «от», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Oh, it was intolerable!” he said, trying to pick up the thread of his interrupted thought. “He does not improve on closer acquaintance. If you want him defined, here he is: a prime, well-fed beast such as takes medals at the cattle shows, and nothing more,” he said, with a tone of vexation that interested her.

cases.explain: «другое образование» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “It’s an utterly different culture—their culture. He’s cultivated, one sees, simply to be able to despise culture, as they despise everything but animal pleasures.”

cases.sentence: – Да ведь вы все любите эти животные удовольствия, – сказала она, и опять он заметил ___, который избегал его.
cases.explain: «мрачный взгляд» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “But don’t you all care for these animal pleasures?” she said, and again he noticed a dark look in her eyes that avoided him.

cases.sentence: Она вытянула лицо и, полузакрыв глаза, быстро изменила выражение лица, сложила руки, и Вронский в ее ___ вдруг увидал то самое выражение лица, с которым поклонился ему Алексей Александрович.
cases.explain: «красивом лице» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: She drew a long face, and half-closing her eyes, quickly transformed her expression, folded her hands, and Vronsky suddenly saw in her beautiful face the very expression with which Alexey Alexandrovitch had bowed to him. He smiled, while she laughed gaily, with that sweet, deep laugh, which was one of her greatest charms.

cases.sentence: Он улыбнулся, а она весело засмеялась тем милым ___, который был одною из главных ее прелестей.
cases.explain: «грудным смехом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: She drew a long face, and half-closing her eyes, quickly transformed her expression, folded her hands, and Vronsky suddenly saw in her beautiful face the very expression with which Alexey Alexandrovitch had bowed to him. He smiled, while she laughed gaily, with that sweet, deep laugh, which was one of her greatest charms.

cases.explain: «министерская машина» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “He’s not a man, not a human being—he’s a doll! No one knows him; but I know him. Oh, if I’d been in his place, I’d long ago have killed, have torn to pieces a wife like me. I wouldn’t have said, ‘Anna, ma chère’! He’s not a man, he’s an official machine. He doesn’t understand that I’m your wife, that he’s outside, that he’s superfluous. … Don’t let’s talk of him! …”

cases.sentence: ___ потух в ее глазах, но другая улыбка – знания чего-то неизвестного ему и тихой грусти – заменила ее прежнее выражение.
cases.explain: «Насмешливый блеск» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: The ironical light died away in her eyes, but a different smile, a consciousness of something, he did not know what, and of quiet melancholy, came over her face.

cases.sentence: – Вот так, вот это лучше, – говорила она, пожимая ___ его руку. – Вот одно, одно, что нам осталось.
cases.explain: «сильным движением» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Yes, it’s better so,” she said, tightly gripping his hand. “That’s the only way, the only way left us.”
